why: §18 lists 'SBOM where available' among the things an independent reviewer needs,
and none existed for this artifact. build/scripts/sbom.sh requires an exported OCI
archive, which is the path that needs tens of gigabytes and is why the security
re-scan failed on its first attempt.
This one was produced by mounting the image's overlay in place (podman create +
podman mount) and cataloguing the mounted directory. Free space measured before
The file is 70 MB and is NOT committed. This project already has a convention for
that -- qualification/tpm/scripts/retain_bulky_evidence.py -- and its rule is the
one followed here: the digest chain runs record -> manifest -> retained bytes on
the builder, so a file that no longer digests to what this manifest claims is not
the file this manifest is about.

note: 'generic' is syft's binary and file cataloguer rather than a package manager, so
it is the largest bucket and the least authoritative. The 1081 rpm entries are the
ones that correspond to what dnf installed; the 560 golang entries are the modules
linked into base-image binaries, which is where every one of the 56 fixable
advisories in the security disposition lives.

reproduce: The script creates a container from the image without starting it, mounts the
overlay, runs `syft scan dir:<mountpoint> -o spdx-json`, and removes both. It is
not deterministic across syft versions and the version above is part of the record
It is also NOT the same instrument as build/scripts/sbom.sh, which catalogues an
oci-archive. The two have not been shown to agree, and a reviewer comparing them
should be told that before they start rather than after.
limitations: Catalogued from a directory, not from an OCI archive. Layer attribution is absent:
this SBOM says what is in the image, not which layer put it there.
The image was mounted read-only in effect but not asserted read-only; nothing wrote
to it, and `podman umount` + `podman rm -f` removed the container afterwards.
